doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Jazz programs in universities
summary: North Texas State's jazz program as a Kenton and Herman farm team, and jazz once forbidden in the conservatory at Pacific.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Jazz is in college. That is so true. You know, do you know what year it was that North Texas State started their jazz program?
I think it was in the mid-60s.
It was in the late 40s right?
Oh the late 40s? Wow. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
I think so. I think around ’49. Because you know for years they were sort of the farm team for Stan Kenton and Woody Herman.
That’s true. You know it took a long time.

And the differences. Because at one time, from the academic standpoint, a conservatory, well at the University of the Pacific, where we went, if you played jazz in the conservatory in the practice room, you could get kicked out. So now it’s just an absolute turnaround. And that’s something too I think most people forget, that that was part of the whole scene in the 50s and in the 60s of trying to get for jazz the same position in the arts as chamber music or symphonies, or any of the arts. To be recognized as an art. And now it is, and so I think we were our own worst enemy because now it’s not part of the general culture that it was in the days of the swing era and the early 50s.
